errors.text_span: The “Vanilla” model (purple, solid line) consistently shows the lowest loss across iterations, ending near 2.5 at 140,000 iterations.
errors.evidence: The statement that the "Vanilla" model consistently shows the lowest loss is an over-generalization as other lines are lower at the beginning. More importantly, the final value is not near 2.5; it is visibly lower, at approximately 2.45.
The final loss for the orange line, “SepLLM (n=64)”, is approximately 2.52, not 2.55.

errors.text_span: The “SepLLM (n=64, H/T)” (red, solid line) and “SepLLM (n=128)” (dark blue, solid line) show slightly higher final losses, around 2.57 and 2.62 respectively
errors.evidence: This statement is incorrect. The chart shows these two models have among the lowest final losses. The red line ends at approximately 2.49, not 2.57. The dark blue line ends at approximately 2.50, not 2.62. The description incorrectly states they have higher final losses when they are actually among the best performing.
The lines are not smooth; they are visibly noisy and jagged, indicating fluctuations in the loss value.
The description fails to mention the shaded areas around each line, which represent variance or confidence intervals and are a prominent feature of the plot.

errors.text_span: indicating a modest performance trade-off for the compression techniques
errors.evidence: This is an interpretive statement about performance trade-offs that goes beyond describing the visual data. Furthermore, it is based on an incorrect reading of the chart data.
